paragraphs: Alliant Energy maintains its principal executive offices in Madison, Wisconsin. Alliant Energy operates as a regulated investor-owned public utility holding company, and its purpose-driven strategy is to serve its customers and build stronger communities. Alliant Energy's primary focus is to provide regulated electric and natural gas service to approximately 1,010,000 electric and approximately 435,000 natural gas customers in the Midwest through its two public utility subsidiaries, IPL and WPL. The primary first tier wholly-owned subsidiaries of Alliant Energy are as follows:

1) IPL - is a public utility engaged principally in the generation and distribution of electricity and the distribution and transportation of natural gas to retail customers in select markets in Iowa. IPL provides utility services to incorporated communities as directed by the IUC and utilizes non-exclusive franchises, which cover the use of public right-of-ways for utility facilities in incorporated communities for a maximum term of 25 years. At December 31, 2025, IPL supplied electric and natural gas service to approximately 505,000 and 230,000 retail customers, respectively, in Iowa. IPL also sells electricity to wholesale customers in Illinois and Iowa and was engaged in the generation and distribution of steam for two customers in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, which were each under contract through 2025 for taking minimum quantities of annual steam usage, with certain conditions. Subsequent to December 31, 2025, IPL exited the steam business.

2) WPL - is a public utility engaged principally in the generation and distribution of electricity and the distribution and transportation of natural gas to retail customers in select markets in Wisconsin. WPL operates in municipalities pursuant to permits of indefinite duration and state statutes authorizing utility operation in areas annexed by a municipality. At December 31, 2025, WPL supplied electric and natural gas service to approximately 505,000 and 205,000 retail customers, respectively. WPL also sells electricity to wholesale customers in Wisconsin.

ATI - currently holds all of Alliant Energy's interest in ATC Holdings. ATC Holdings is comprised of a 16% ownership interest in ATC and a 20% ownership interest in ATC Holdco LLC. ATC is an independent, for-profit, transmission-only company. ATC Holdco LLC holds an interest in Duke-American Transmission Company, LLC, which holds a note receivable related to the previously owned electric transmission infrastructure in North America.

Corporate Venture Investments - includes various minority ownership interests in regional and national venture funds, including a global coalition of energy companies working together to help identify and research innovative technologies and business models within the emerging energy economy.
Non-utility Wind Farm - includes a 50% cash equity ownership interest in a 225 MW non-utility wind farm located in Oklahoma.

Sheboygan Falls Energy Facility - is a 347 MW, simple-cycle, natural gas-fired EGU near Sheboygan Falls, Wisconsin, which is currently leased to WPL through 2044. Refer to Note 9 for additional information on WPL's Sheboygan Falls Energy Facility lease.

Travero - is a supply chain solutions company, including a short-line rail freight service in Iowa; a Mississippi River barge, rail and truck freight terminal in Illinois; freight brokerage services; and a rail-served warehouse in Iowa.

Development-ready Sites - includes various rail-served and ready-to-build manufacturing and industrial sites throughout Alliant Energy's service territories, with access to various airports and interstate freeways.

paragraphs: You should carefully consider each of the risks described below relating to Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL, together with all of the other information contained in this combined report, before making an investment decision with respect to our securities. If any of the following risks develop into actual events, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

Demand from data centers and other large load growth customers may impact our business - Our ability to manage the development and implementation of complex business opportunities related to the growing demand for data centers may be limited by financial, operational, or regulatory factors. We may enter into agreements requiring significant capital investment in generation and transmission capacity for large load growth customers before realizing any potential returns. We may not be able to affordably and timely construct generation, or cause transmission companies to affordably and timely construct transmission infrastructure to meet potential load growth from any large load growth customer. A large load growth customer may decide not to take energy, take less energy than anticipated, or not take service on the anticipated schedule, due to changes in business needs, construction delays, technological advances that improve energy efficiency, or other factors, which may result in lower demand for energy than anticipated. The addition of large load growth customers may increase the concentration of sales, and increase revenue and earnings volatility. We may not be able to adequately protect against the risks inherent in relying on rapid growth within a small number of large customers in a single industry. The inability or delays in obtaining regulatory approvals with acceptable conditions or providing sufficient generation or securing transmission, due to supply chain risk, operational risk, or other factors, may impact our ability, or the cost, to provide energy to new customers. The individual customer rates may not provide sufficient revenues to fully recover the costs, the contracts with large load growth customers may increase counterparty credit risk, and the costs to provide service may be higher than expected. Large load growth customers may not be able to meet obligations in our contracts, including the obligation to pay any termination charges. Additionally, if pipeline expansions needed for new gas‑fired generation are delayed or not approved, we may be unable to meet peak requirements for data center load, increasing market purchases or capacity procurement costs. Any of these circumstances could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and growth prospects.

Laws, regulations, and opposition to data centers may impact our business - Federal, state or local legislation, rulemaking, or siting standards that specifically restrict or delay the zoning, siting or operation of data centers could reduce or defer expected load growth and impair cost recovery for associated infrastructure. Community opposition to data centers—driven by concerns about land use, water consumption, generation emissions, noise, or traffic—could result in permitting delays, litigation, project cancellations, or additional mitigation costs, reducing expected load growth. The ability to serve significant new commercial or industrial customers on contract rates, including data centers, may require certain regulatory approvals, and the activities and costs related to the construction, acquisition or contracts for additional generation capacity and transmission required to meet the high demands of such customers could be significant. The individual customer rates for large load growth customers are subject to regulatory approvals and our regulatory authorities may change the rates we can charge and the costs that can be recovered. As a result, we may experience adverse impacts on our financial condition and results of operations.

Our utility business is significantly impacted by government legislation, regulation and oversight - Our utility financial condition is influenced by how regulatory authorities, including the IUC, the PSCW and FERC, establish the rates we can charge our customers, our authorized rates of return and common equity levels, and the costs that may be recovered from customers. Our ability to timely obtain rate adjustments to earn authorized rates of return depends upon timely regulatory action under applicable statutes and regulations, and cannot be guaranteed. IPL and WPL may not receive an adequate amount of rate relief to recover all costs and earn their authorized rates of return, rates may be reduced, rate refunds may be required, rate adjustments may not be approved on a timely basis, costs may not be otherwise recovered through rates, earnings above certain thresholds may be required to be refunded or be used to reduce existing rate base of assets with higher levels of authorized return on equity, recovery of capital expenditures, including those for electric distribution systems, above certain thresholds may be capped or not be allowed, rates may be temporarily frozen, such as IPL's current retail electric rate base moratorium through September 2029, laws, rules or settlements may limit the ability to file rate adjustments or the period covered by a rate adjustment, regulatory decisions may limit the ability to defer recovery of and a return on prudently incurred costs in between rate reviews, certain rate base items may not receive a full weighted average cost of capital, and authorized rates of return on capital may be reduced. As a result, we may experience adverse impacts on our financial condition and results of operations.

In addition, our operations are subject to extensive regulation primarily by the IUC, the PSCW and FERC. We are also subject to oversight and monitoring by organizations such as the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, the Midwest Reliability Organization, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration, the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO) and the Department of Homeland Security Transportation Security Administration. The impacts on our operations include: our ability to site and construct new energy facilities, such as renewable energy, energy storage projects, or natural gas-fired electric generating units (EGUs), and recover associated costs; our ability to decommission generating facilities and recover related costs and the remaining carrying value of these facilities and related assets; MISO's resource adequacy process establishing seasonal capacity planning reserve margin and capacity accreditation requirements, as well as additional changes to capacity accreditation, such as the direct loss of load methodology, impact how and when existing and new generating facilities such as IPL's and WPL's additional solar generation are accredited with energy capacity, and may require IPL and WPL to adjust their current resource plans, to add resources to meet the requirements of MISO's seasonal resource adequacy process, or procure capacity whereby such costs might not be recovered in rates; legislation or regulation that imposes mandatory integrated resource planning requirements, or materially changes existing resource planning standards, could delay approvals, require revisions to resource plans, increase compliance costs, and impact our ability to timely meet demand for energy from commercial and industrial customers, including data centers; the impact of the lack of availability of existing and new generating facilities on our accredited capacity for such facilities pursuant to MISO's seasonal resource adequacy process; IPL's ability to achieve certain aggregate summer capacity factors under the consumer protection plan for its up to 400 MW of solar generation projects; the rates paid to transmission operators and how those costs are recovered from customers, including our ability to continue to use a transmission rider in Iowa; our ability to site, construct and recover costs for new natural gas pipelines; our ability to recover costs to upgrade our electric and gas distribution systems; the amount of certain sources of energy we must use, such as renewable sources; our ability to purchase generating facilities and recover the costs associated therewith; our ability to sell utility assets and any conditions placed upon the sale of such assets; our ability to enter into purchased power agreements and recover the costs associated therewith; the allocation of expenditures by transmission companies on transmission network upgrades and our ability to recover costs associated therewith; reliability; safety; the issuance of securities and ability to use other financing arrangements for our renewable energy projects; accounting matters; and transactions between affiliates. These regulatory authorities and organizations are also empowered to impose financial penalties and other sanctions, including requirements to implement new compliance programs. Failure to obtain approvals for any of these matters in a timely manner, or receipt of approvals with uneconomical conditions, may cause us not to pursue the construction of such projects, or to record an impairment of our assets, or may cause a delay in construction of such projects such that we are not able to meet new demand growth, and may have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations. Legislative or regulatory changes that enable large load growth customers, including data centers, to own or procure on-site generation or to self-supply through sources behind-the-meter or behind-the-meter arrangements could materially reduce retail sales, shift cost recovery to remaining customers, and impact our ability to earn authorized rates of return. Changes to these regulations could materially increase our costs or cause us to reconsider our strategy, which could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.

Provisions of the Wisconsin Utility Holding Company Act may limit our ability to invest in or grow our non-utility activities and may deter potential purchasers who might be willing to pay a premium for our stock.

paragraphs: This MDA includes information relating to Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL (collectively, the Utilities), as well as ATC Holdings, AEF and Corporate Services. Where appropriate, information relating to a specific entity has been segregated and labeled as such. The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the Financial Statements and Notes included in this report. Unless otherwise noted, all "per share" references in MDA refer to earnings per diluted share. In addition, this MDA includes certain financial information for 2025 compared to 2024. Refer to MDA in the combined 2024 Form 10-K for details on certain financial information for 2024 compared to 2023.

Alliant Energy's mission is to deliver the energy solutions and exceptional service that its customers and communities count on - affordably, safely, reliably and responsibly. This mission aligns with Alliant Energy's purpose - to serve customers and build stronger communities - which guides it through the evolving dynamics of the economy and the energy industry. Alliant Energy leads as a corporate citizen, advancing environmental stewardship and supporting the communities in its service territories. Alliant Energy's mission and purpose are supported by a strategy focused on meeting evolving customer expectations, delivering attractive returns for investors, and advancing emerging technologies and generation to enable safe, secure and future-ready energy production. This strategy includes the following key elements:

Providing affordable energy solutions for customers - Alliant Energy's strategy focuses on affordable energy solutions that support retention and growth of existing customers and attract new customers to its service territories.

•Alliant Energy's resource plan is the roadmap for building a strong and resilient energy future to meet the growing energy needs across Iowa and Wisconsin. This long-term plan expands generation capacity and includes a balanced mix of natural gas, energy storage, new renewable generation, improvements at existing natural gas-fired EGUs and refurbishments at existing wind farms. It is designed to deliver the reliable, affordable energy customers count on by efficiently increasing the capabilities of existing generation through gas and wind facility upgrades while also building larger scale natural gas facilities to capture economies of scale. Alliant Energy's industry-leading wind and solar energy resources provide zero-fuel cost generation as well as generate renewable tax credits that are provided to its electric customers. By enhancing new and existing energy sources while maximizing traditional energy sources, Alliant Energy is helping support economic growth, maintain reliability and keep customer bills affordable. At the same time, Alliant Energy is modernizing its distribution system to create a smarter, more adaptable infrastructure that increases resiliency and supports evolving energy technologies. By advancing a responsible approach to energy resources, Alliant Energy can deliver what matters most to the customers and communities it serves - affordably, safely and reliably.

•Higher electric capacity revenues from existing generation resources beginning in 2025 are expected to provide cost benefits to WPL's retail electric customers in the future through its fuel cost recovery mechanism.

•Alliant Energy, IPL and WPL have utilized, and expect to continue to utilize, various provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 to enhance tax benefits provided to customers that are expected from wind, solar and energy storage projects in Iowa and Wisconsin, including transferring certain future tax credits from such projects to other corporate taxpayers. Refer to Note 1(c) for discussion of $285 million, $216 million and $98 million of proceeds from renewable tax credits transferred to other corporate taxpayers in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

•Reductions in Iowa corporate income tax rates resulting from tax reform enacted in 2022 are expected to provide cost benefits to IPL's electric and gas customers in the future. IPL's retail electric and gas customers began receiving these benefits with the new base rates effective October 1, 2024.

•IPL provided billing credits to its retail electric customers through the tax benefit rider of $52 million and $16 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. IPL also provided its retail electric customers $162 million and $40 million in credits on customers' bills related to production tax credits through its fuel-related cost recovery mechanism in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

•IPL maintaining flat base rates for its retail electric and gas customers from 2021 through September 30, 2024, as well as a retail electric base rate moratorium from October 2025 through September 2029 approved by the IUC in IPL's most recent retail electric rate review.

•Completion of a restructuring and voluntary employee separation program in 2024, which is expected to reduce operation and maintenance expenses in the future. Refer to Note 12 for discussion of this program.

•IPL and WPL have entered into conditional commitments with the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Energy Dominance Financing, formerly the Loan Programs Office, for loan guarantees of approximately $1.4 billion and $1.6 billion, respectively. If finalized, such loans would provide low interest financing for IPL's and WPL's expected construction of eligible projects as defined in the governing agreement.

•In July 2024, the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Electricity - formerly administered by the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations awarded WPL's Columbia Energy Storage Project, an approximately 20 MW compressed CO2-based long-duration energy storage system at the Columbia Energy Center site, up to approximately $30 million in grant funding during construction of the project.

•In April 2025, WPL submitted an application to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers for up to $45 million in loans through the Corps Water Infrastructure Financing Program. If finalized, such loans would provide low interest financing for various proposed safety projects at WPL's Kilbourn and Prairie du Sac hydro EGUs.

•IPL and WPL executed agreements to enable fiber connectivity to one of its data center customers by leasing underground conduit in their service territories, which is expected to provide cost benefits to IPL's and WPL's existing customers.

paragraphs: Alliant Energy 位於威斯康辛州麥迪遜市設有主要營業據點。Alliant Energy 係一間受監管的投資人所有公共電力公用事業控股公司，其以服務客戶與建設更強大社區為導向的策略。Alliant Energy 的主要業務為透過其兩間公共電力子公司 IPL 與 WPL，為美國中西部地區約 1,010,000 戶電力用戶與約 435,000 戶天然氣用戶提供受監管的電力與天然氣服務。Alliant Energy 的主要一級全資子公司如下：

1) IPL - 為一間公共電力公司，主要從事電力的發電與配電，以及天然氣的配電與輸送至愛荷華州特定市場的零售用戶。IPL 根據 IUC 的指示為已設立社區提供電力服務，並使用非獨佔性特許權，該特許權允許在已設立社區內使用公共道路權為電力設施，期限為最多 25 年。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，IPL 為愛荷華州約 505,000 戶電力用戶與 230,000 戶天然氣用戶提供服務。IPL 遠售電力至伊利諾州與愛荷華州的批發用戶，並曾為愛荷華州西德雷福斯的兩位用戶提供蒸汽的發電與配電服務，該兩位用戶均與 IPL 簽訂合約，至 2025 年為止需採購最低年度蒸汽用量，並附有特定條件。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之後，IPL 已退出蒸汽業務。
2) WPL - 為一間公共電力公司，主要從事電力的發電與配電，以及天然氣的配電與輸送至威斯康辛州特定市場的零售用戶。WPL 根據無限期許可與州法律授權在各市轄區內運營電力業務。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，WPL 為威斯康辛州約 505,000 戶電力用戶與 205,000 戶天然氣用戶提供服務。WPL 亦遠售電力至威斯康辛州的批發用戶。

ATI - 目前持有 Alliant Energy 在 ATC Holdings 的全部權益。ATC Holdings 包含對 ATC 的 16% 股權與對 ATC Holdco LLC 的 20% 股權。ATC 為一間獨立、營利性、僅從事電力傳輸的公司。ATC Holdco LLC 持有對 Duke-American Transmission Company, LLC 的權益，該公司持有與北美先前所有電力傳輸基礎設施相關的應收款。
企業風險投資 - 包含對區域與國家級風險基金的多數股權，包括一個全球能源公司聯盟，共同合作以識別與研究新興能源經濟中的創新技術與商業模式。
非電力風力發電廠 - 包含對位於奧克拉荷馬州、裝置容量為 225 MW 的非電力風力發電廠的 50% 現金股權。
Sheboygan Falls 能源設施 - 為一間位於威斯康辛州 Sheboygan Falls 頑近、裝置容量為 347 MW 的簡單循環天然氣燃氣發電廠（EGU），目前租賃給 WPL 至 2044 年為止。有關 WPL 的 Sheboygan Falls 能源設施租賃，請參閱第九節附註。
Travero - 為一間供應鏈解決方案公司，包括在愛荷華州的短線鐵路貨運服務；在伊利諾州的密西西比河船運、鐵路與卡車貨運碼頭；貨運經紀服務；以及在愛荷華州的鐵路服務倉庫。
Development-ready Sites - 包含各種鐵路服務且已準備好建設的製造與工業用地，遍及 Alliant Energy 服務區域，並可接駁多種機場與州際高速公路。

paragraphs: 此 MDA 包含與 Alliant Energy、IPL 以及 WPL（合稱為「電力公司」）相關之資訊，以及 ATC Holdings、AEF 及 Corporate Services。於適當之情形，與特定實體相關之資訊已分離並標示為該實體。以下討論與分析應與本報告所包含之財務報表及附註同時閱讀。除非另有說明，所有「每股」參考資訊均指稀釋後每股盈餘。此外，此 MDA 包含 2025 年與 2024 年之部分財務資訊。有關 2024 年與 2023 年財務資訊之詳細資訊，請參閱合併 2024 年 Form 10-K 中之 MDA。

Alliant Energy 之使命為提供客戶與社區所倚賴的能源解決方案與卓越服務 - 以可負擔、安全、可靠且負責任的方式。此使命與 Alliant Energy 之宗旨 - 服務客戶並建設更強大之社區 - 一致，此宗旨引導其應對經濟與能源產業的變動。Alliant Energy 作為企業公民領導，推進環境管理並支持其服務地區之社區。Alliant Energy 之使命與宗旨由一項策略支撐，該策略聚焦於應對客戶需求的變遷、為投資者提供具吸引力之回報，以及推進新興科技與發電，以實現安全、穩健且未來準備就緒之能源生產。此策略包含以下關鍵要素：
提供可負擔之能源解決方案給客戶 - Alliant Energy 之策略聚焦於可負擔之能源解決方案，以支持現有客戶之留存與成長並吸引新客戶至其服務地區。

•Alliant Energy 之資源計畫為建立強而有韌性之能源未來的路線圖，以應對愛荷華州與威斯康辛州日益增長之能源需求。此長期計畫擴充發電容量，並包含天然氣、能源儲存、新可再生能源發電、現有天然氣發電廠之改善以及現有風電場之翻新。此計畫設計為透過天然氣與風電設施之升級，提高現有發電能力之效率，同時建設更大規模之天然氣設施以取得規模經濟效益。Alliant Energy 之行業領先風能與太陽能資源提供零燃料成本發電，並產生可再生能源稅額抵減，提供給其電力客戶。透過增強新舊能源來源，同時最大化傳統能源來源，Alliant Energy 正協助支持經濟成長、維持可靠性並保持客戶費用可負擔。同時，Alliant Energy 正現代化其配電系統，以建立更智慧且更具適應力之基礎設施，提高韌性並支持能源科技之變遷。透過推進對能源資源負責任的態度，Alliant Energy 可以提供其服務之客戶與社區最重要之東西 - 可負擔、安全且可靠。
•自 2025 年起，來自現有發電資源之電力容量收入增加，預期將透過 WPL 之燃料成本回復機制，為其零售電力客戶帶來成本效益。

•Alliant Energy、IPL 以及 WPL 已利用並預期將持續利用 2022 年《通貨膨脹減緩法案》之各項條款，以增強預期來自愛荷華州與威斯康辛州風能、太陽能與能源儲存專案之客戶稅額利益，包括將某些專案未來稅額抵減轉讓至其他企業納稅人。有關 2025 年、2024 年與 2023 年分別轉讓至其他企業納稅人之 2.85 億美元、2.16 億美元與 9,800 萬美元之可再生能源稅額抵減所得金額之討論，請參閱附註 1(c)。
•愛荷華州企業所得稅率因 2022 年稅制改革而降低，預期將為 IPL 之電力與天然氣客戶帶來成本效益。IPL 之零售電力與天然氣客戶自 2024 年 10 月 1 日生效之新基準費率開始享有此項效益。
•IPL 於 2025 年與 2024 年分別透過稅益 rider 提供其零售電力客戶 5,200 萬美元與 1,600 萬美元之帳單信用。IPL 亦透過其燃料相關成本回復機制，於 2025 年與 2024 年分別為其零售電力客戶提供 1.62 億美元與 4,000 萬美元之帳單信用，與生產稅額抵減相關。
•IPL 保持零售電力與天然氣客戶的基礎費率不變，自 2021 年至 2024 年 9 月 30 日，以及自 2025 年 10 月起至 2029 年 9 月止的零售電力基礎費率禁令，此禁令已獲 IPL 最近一次零售電力費率審查中 IUC 批准。
•於 2024 年完成一項重整及自願員工離職計畫，預期將未來降低運作與維護費用。有關此計畫之討論，請參閱附註 12。
•IPL 與 WPL 已與美國能源部能源主導融資辦公室（ formerly the Loan Programs Office）簽訂條件性承諾，為其各自預計提供約 14 億美元與 16 億美元的貸款擔保。若該貸款最終確定，將為 IPL 與 WPL 預期建設符合規定之項目提供低利率融資。
•於 2024 年 7 月，美國能源部電力辦公室（ formerly 管理於清潔能源示範辦公室）已批准 WPL 的 Columbia 能源儲存計畫，該計畫為位於 Columbia 能源中心的約 20 MW 壓縮二氧化碳基長時儲能系統，預計在建設期間提供約 3,000 萬美元的補助金。
•於 2025 年 4 月，WPL 向美國陸軍工程兵 Corps of Engineers 提交申請，申請透過 Corps 水基礎設施融資計畫提供最高 4,500 萬美元貸款。若該貸款最終確定，將為 WPL 在 Kilbourn 與 Prairie du Sac 水電廠所提出的多項安全計畫提供低利率融資。
•IPL 與 WPL 已簽訂協議，透過出租其服務區域內的地下導管，為其資料中心客戶提供光纖連線，預期將為 IPL 與 WPL 現有客戶帶來成本效益。

paragraphs: 您應仔細審慎評估下列所有與 Alliant Energy、IPL 及 WPL 有關的風險，以及本合併報告中所包含的所有其他資訊，再做投資決策。若任何上述風險成為實際事件，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響，您可能損失全部或部分投資。

資料中心及其他大型負載成長客戶的需求可能影響本公司業務 - 本公司管理與複雜商業機會相關的發展與落實能力，可能受到財務、營運或法規因素的限制。本公司可能與大型負載成長客戶簽訂協議，要求進行大量資本投資以建設發電與輸電容量，而在實現任何潛在回報前。本公司可能無法以可負擔且及時的方式建設發電設施，或促使輸電公司以可負擔且及時的方式建設輸電基礎設施，以應對任何大型負載成長客戶的潛在負載成長。大型負載成長客戶可能因業務需求變更、建設延誤、技術進步提高能源效率或其他因素，決定不採用能源、採用較少能源，或未按預期時間表提供服務，這可能導致能源需求低於預期。大型負載成長客戶的加入可能增加銷售集中度，並提高營收與獲利的波動性。本公司可能無法充分對抗依賴少數大型客戶在單一產業中快速成長所內含的風險。因供應鏈風險、營運風險或其他因素，無法取得或延誤取得符合可接受條件的法規核准、提供足夠發電或確保輸電，可能影響本公司或輸電公司提供能源給新客戶的能力或成本。個別客戶的電價可能無法充分回收成本，與大型負載成長客戶的契約可能增加交易對手信用風險，且提供服務的成本可能高於預期。大型負載成長客戶可能無法履行本公司契約中的義務，包括支付任何終止費用。此外，若用於新氣體發電的管線擴建延誤或未獲批准，本公司可能無法滿足資料中心負載的高峯需求，增加市場採購或容量採購成本。任何上述情況都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果與成長前景造成不利影響。

法律、法規與對資料中心的反對可能影響本公司業務 - 聯邦、州或地方立法、規則制定或設置標準，若明確限制或延宕資料中心的 zoning、設置或運作，可能減少或延後預期負載成長，並影響相關基礎設施的成本回收。社區對資料中心的反對，因土地使用、用水、發電排放、噪音或交通等問題，可能導致許可延宕、訴訟、項目取消或額外緩衝成本，減少預期負載成長。為服務重要的新商業或工業客戶（包括資料中心）在契約電價上，可能需要特定法規核准，且與建設、取得或契約額外發電容量及輸電所需的活動與成本可能相當重大。大型負載成長客戶的個別電價需經法規核准，且本公司法規機關可能改變我們可收取的電價與可回收的成本。因此，我們可能面臨對財務狀況與營運成果的不利影響。

本公司電力業務大幅受政府立法、法規與監督影響 - 本公司電力財務狀況受影響，取決於包括 IUC、PSCW 與 FERC 在內的法規機關如何設定我們可向客戶收取的電價、核准的回報率與普通股比例，以及可從客戶回收的成本。我們及時取得電價調整以賺取核准回報率的能力，取決於適用法律與法規下的及時法規行動，且無法保證。IPL 與 WPL 可能無法獲得足夠的電價減免以回收所有成本並賺取核准回報率，電價可能降低，電價退款可能被要求，電價調整可能未在及時基礎上核准，成本可能無法透過電價回收，超過特定門檻的獲利可能被要求退款或用以減少現有資產的電價基數，回收資本支出（包括電力配電系統的資本支出）若超過特定門檻可能被限制或不允許，電價可能暫時凍結，例如 IPL 目前的零售電力電價基數凍結至 2029 年 9 月，法律、規則或和解可能限制提出電價調整或電價調整所涵蓋的期間，法規決策可能限制延後回收及回報於審查之間的審慎支出，某些電價基數項目可能無法獲得完整的加權平均資金成本，核准的資本回報率可能降低。因此，我們可能面臨對財務狀況與營運成果的不利影響。

此外，本公司營運受廣泛法規監督，主要由 IUC、PSCW 與 FERC 管理。我們也受組織如北美電力可靠性委員會、中西部可靠性組織、管線與危險材料安全管理局、中西部獨立系統運營商（MISO）與國土安全部運輸安全管理局的監督與監測。對本公司營運的影響包括：我們設置與建設新能源設施（如再生能源、能源儲存項目或天然氣發電單位）並回收相關成本的能力；我們關閉發電設施並回收相關成本與這些設施及相關資產的剩餘帳面價值的能力；MISO 的資源充足性程序建立季節性容量規劃儲備邊際與容量認證要求，以及對容量認證的其他變更，如直接負載損失方法，影響如何及何時認證現有與新發電設施（如 IPL 與 WPL 的額外太陽能發電）的能源容量，並可能要求 IPL 與 WPL 調整其當前資源計畫，以增加資源以符合 MISO 的季節性資源充足性程序要求，或採購容量，使得相關成本可能無法透過電價回收；立法或法規若強制執行整合資源規劃要求，或大幅改變現有資源規劃標準，可能延宕核准、要求修訂資源計畫、增加合規成本，並影響我們及時滿足商業與工業客戶（包括資料中心）能源需求的能力；缺乏現有與新發電設施的可用性對我們根據 MISO 季節性資源充足性程序認證這些設施的認證容量的影響；IPL 達成其至多 400 MW 太陽能發電專案的總夏季容量因子的能力；支付給輸電運營商的電價與如何從客戶回收這些成本，包括我們持續使用愛荷華州的輸電 rider 的能力；我們設置、建設與回收新天然氣管線成本的能力；我們回收升級電力與天然氣配電系統成本的能力；我們必須使用的某些能源來源的數量，如可再生能源；我們購買發電設施並回收相關成本的能力；我們出售電力資產與出售這些資產所附帶的條件；我們與第三方簽訂購電協議並回收相關成本的能力；輸電公司對輸電網路升級的支出分配與我們回收相關成本的能力；可靠性；安全性；發行證券與使用其他融資安排進行可再生能源專案的能力；會計事項；以及關聯方之間的交易。這些法規機關與組織也有權處以財務處罰或其他處分，包括要求實施新的合規計畫。未能及時取得這些事項的核准，或取得核准時附有不經濟的條件，可能導致我們不進行這些專案的建設，或需記提資產減損，或導致這些專案建設延誤，使得我們無法滿足新的負載成長，並可能對我們的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。立法或法規變動若使大型負載成長客戶（包括資料中心）能擁有或採購廠內發電或透過廠內電源或廠內電源安排自給自足，可能大幅減少零售銷售，將成本回收轉移至剩餘客戶，並影響我們賺取核准回報率的能力。這些法規的變動可能大幅增加我們的成本，或使我們重新考慮策略，這可能對我們的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
威斯康辛州電力控股公司法的條款可能限制我們投資或成長非電力業務的能力，並可能阻卻潛在買家願意以較高價格購入我們股票的意願。
